# Affine proof cores and incremental machine transport

21 October 2026. New research packet; earlier delivered packets are preserved.

## Read first

report.pdf summarizes the new findings, recent archive status and limits. The new reusable macro interface contracts 1,059 exact drain loops into a 367-vertex affine core with 33 shared matrices. This is not a TM state reduction. For the currently identical source graphs, direct normalized/canonical equality is simpler; contraction adds checks and may add overhead. Its strongest use is comparison of future differing loop implementations.

The exact context215 patch is an independently checked six-block instance of an ALREADY KNOWN old-run positive-stutter method. Nine old-table graph histories suffice; arbitrary initial tape equivalence reuses startup. FM215/M124 use fewer local blocks/marker facts but still need upstream semantic adapters. CM215 has the least remaining Lean integration work: its Core attachment is recorded compiled, while its final ZFC adapter closure is explicitly not freshly compiled. No new compiled context215 theorem is claimed.

The new model patch removes three formula inductions (270 to 235 lines). All new formal proposals remain uncompiled. Recent incoming archives do contain recorded compiled normalized and zero-offset source lanes, but maintained Lean/Coq subtrees are unchanged through main 62f0f95e2b2df5b380ae502eb65bd64f1ee90209. Archive proof records are not a fresh local full-endpoint build.

## Portable replay

Python 3 standard library only, assertions enabled, using a fresh external directory:

    python -I -B verify.py --work /tmp/next-proof-check

The verifier regenerates the complete canonical input graph from pinned Lean literals, checks current tree equality, recomputes drain contraction, ranks, shared matrices, auxiliary quotient/interval results and adversarial tests. It checks six whole-tape patch blocks, old-only histories, malformed-patch rejection, decoder products and the complete DR row-dependency census. The DR analyzer assumes existing BoxLemmas; unchanged direct row footprints do not alone establish formal oracle reuse. Logical proposed-source hashes and removed induction names are checked, not compiled.

All generated outputs are written to copies in the external work directory. None of the received Lean/Rocq sources or archived scripts are executed. Owned Python checkers operate on inert data. Structural and runtime scripts reject optimized Python. graph_origin is the earlier owned source-to-graph audit, included so that contraction's input need not be trusted as an unexplained JSON file.

## Contents and provenance

- structural: complete original/affine graphs, local drain certificates, ranks, shared matrices, independent validator, mutations and scoped negative analyses.
- runtime: exact old/new context tables, patch certificate/checker, decoder inputs and certificates, DR affected-guard receipt and owned replay.
- calculus: uncompiled exact patch and generic transport/projection proposals with pinned source excerpts.
- review: current commit/subtree receipts, recorded archive source/log hash audits, and two relevant incoming proof archives as INERT evidence.
- graph_origin: pinned source-tree literals and owned canonical graph checker with exact wrapping pointer semantics.
- licenses: inherited source notices/pins retained; new scripts are owned research validators. No external dependency installation or network access is required by replay.

The top manifest pins every payload, including nested manifests. Archive status records have not been independently recompiled. To build report.tex, run pdflatex twice with geometry, lmodern, amsmath, amssymb, booktabs and hyperref. The delivered PDF is separately rendered and visually checked.

# Recent-commit runtime proof simplification

The inputs correspond to main commit53269bcab1efc0f82d3022645bd7cf0c22d84959. The context-return and shallow bytes were independently matched to that intake. The literal tables and source files are pinned in pins.json and the file manifest. Everything executed here is owned checking code, not received repository scripts.

Recommended first read: PROOF_DESIGN.md. The main independently checked application is a one-sided-history patch theorem transporting the existing K215 endpoint to context215, avoiding a new source proof,6,176 site proofs and a separate initializer proof. Six short blocks and nine old-table history paths suffice. The all-initial-tapes strengthening and elimination of new-table history obligations are independently checked simplifications of the supplied block argument, not a claim to have invented generic stuttering equivalence.

Run:
- python check_patch.py
- python test_patch.py
- python check_decoder.py
- python check_dr_delta.py

The first three finish quickly. The DR dependency census takes several seconds and records an exact direct evaluator footprint. All use only the Python standard library.

check_decoder.py checks every local template with opaque exterior, and the entire source-node/physical-state/two-bit-history coverage product. It does not discharge generic leaf-return obligations. check_dr_delta.py assumes the corresponding BoxLemmas, following the previously inspected Lean symbolic rules; formal reuse of unchanged oracle theorems requires their dependency footprint separately. No new Lean/Rocq compilation or measured proof-assistant speedup is claimed.

Results: context215 and shallow215 have the SAME decoder interface counts as certified K215; DR215 has one more product state than ST215. These alternative tables do not offer a smaller standalone physical-runtime theorem by that metric. The context variant nevertheless has an exceptionally small incremental transport proof. DR's two modified rows affect139 guarded executions, not merely the four changed source operands, so direct reuse should recheck139 and transport6,012 after proving the dependency theorem.

## Attribution and comparison with newly received transport archives

The incoming FM215 and M124 archives already describe old-run-only positive stuttering, arbitrary-initial-tape equivalence at control0, and reuse of the baseline endpoint without new runtime or startup proofs. The M124 comparison explicitly identifies the context-return alternative as a larger multi-block case. Therefore the present result is an independently checked instantiation and obligation count, NOT a claim to invent generic stuttering, one-sided-history transport, or all-tape strengthening.

FM215/M124 need two incoming-marker facts and two three-step blocks, fewer obligations than the context-return certificate's six blocks and nine incoming graph histories. Subject to verifying their table binding and reported formal compilation, they have smaller local proof obligations, but this alone does not establish the least remaining endpoint-integration work. The context-return checker remains a useful generic multi-block certificate test and independently checks the committed table. Incoming compiler logs were not executed or independently reproduced by this checker.

## Final recommendation: attachment completeness outweighs clause count

CM215 currently has the least remaining work to inherit the maintained Lean K215 endpoint. The archive named K215_Proof_Simplification_2026-10-21 (2) contains CM215Core.blank_halts_iff_primary in the repository's actual Machine215/KDenseBridge.BlankHalts semantics. Its archived compilation records cover the exact430-row compatibility checks, the CoreNativeBridge representation theorem and this exact-machine equivalence, with reported axioms propext and Quot.sound. CM215ZFCAdapter.lean already imports KEndpoint215 and composes blank_halts_iff_zfc_refutation, but explicitly was not included in the fresh full-endpoint build. Another CM transport archive independently records compiled CM215Dense/core bridge and likewise provides an uncompiled final integration wrapper.

Minimal remaining CM obligation: place/rebuild the supplied adapter against the maintained endpoint dependency closure, verify exact module/table bindings and inspect its final assumptions. No new representation theorem or runtime-site proof is indicated by these records. This is the closest supplied adapter, not a claim that the complete alternative ZFC endpoint has already been rebuilt.

FM215 has a shorter local proof and an archived successful Lean all_tapes_halts_iff theorem, but its theorem uses standalone integer/function-tape configurations. The supplied FM proof does not contain a compiled adapter to the repository's Machine215/KDenseBridge.BlankHalts endpoint. Minimal remaining FM obligations: instantiate or adapt a generic representation bridge, bind both exact literal tables and start/halt labels, then compose and compile the final maintained endpoint. The existing generic CM bridge may be reusable, but reuse itself must be checked.

M124 similarly has standalone all-tape exact-table equivalence in both Lean and Rocq. The Rocq receipt reports closed assumptions and successful coqchk; the Lean receipt lists propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Both explicitly exclude integration with the upstream ZFC endpoint model. Minimal remaining M124 obligations: on Lean, the same exact table/model bridge plus endpoint composition; on Rocq, a stream-zipper/BusyCoq-to-integer-tape bridge with the native301→102,302→120,254→230 map, OR port the short local marker proof directly into the existing BusyCoq semantics, then compose with CorrectDense215.

Therefore distinguish two answers: FM/M124 have the simpler local marker argument; CM has the most complete supplied compiled attachment and is presently the best near-term endpoint-integration choice. None removes the inherited K215 logical/calculus dependency closure. Archived records were inspected, not recompiled by this audit. ADAPTER_AUDIT.json pins the precise sources and records used.

# Verified certificate refinements for K215

Research and integration packet, 21 October 2026.

Repository snapshot:
`53269bcab1efc0f82d3022645bd7cf0c22d84959` of
[VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt](https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt).
The research includes all seven ZIP proposals in `docs/incoming` at that pin.

## Results

1. **Exact source proof with balanced certificate lookup.**
   `Source215Balanced.p215_dagPerm_balanced` proves, for every register file
   `R`, `rm_halts p215 ([], R) <-> rm_halts dagPerm ([], R)`.
   The new tree checker is proved equal to the inherited ordinary checker.
   The exact 2,240-entry certificate gives 54,514 lookup-node visits versus
   5,018,706 with list indexing. This is a count of one component, not a
   92-fold runtime claim. A single local timing was lower; tree construction
   adds cost, so no whole-build speedup is claimed.
2. **One generic finite checker for M124, FM215, and provider-125 M125.**
   The checked theorem gives arbitrary-tape halting equivalence with the exact
   primary K215. Three literal instances use the same two-clause invariant.
   M125 native and dense tables are supplied. Provider 125 was already
   suggested in the M124 incoming note; no novelty claim is made for the idea.
3. **Concrete zero-credit enumeration theorem.**
   `CantorCredit.v` proves the actual Cantor encoding and decoder, the strict
   NIP-to-DROP occurrence injection, and protected credit for the literal
   increasing raw-code schedule. The mathematical injection is prior work;
   the new contribution closes the concrete codec and scheduler hypotheses.
4. **No 214-state machine found.**
   A reproducible restricted fold search covered 21 tables, 155,277
   pair/table combinations, and 133,827,040 replacement-action checks.
   No complete fold passed. This supplies no lower bound and is not a count
   of distinct complete machines.

All delivered machines have **215 working states**, a separate halt, one
binary two-way tape, L/R moves, and initialization included.

## Read first

`report.pdf` is the complete report; `report.tex` and `sections/*.tex` are its
editable source. The report distinguishes existing proposals, new compiled
results, finite corroboration, and future integration work.

| Directory | Purpose |

| `balanced_lookup/` | Generic lookup refinement, exact source theorem, minimal inherited dependencies, measurements and compiler receipts |
| `marker_certificate/` | Generic table checker, three compiled instances, literal tables and finite audits |
| `zero_credit/` | Concrete scheduler theorem, candidate comparison, incoming inventory and independent marker review |
| `state_search/` | Restricted search implementation, controls, counts, provenance and explicit-table inventory |
| `evidence/` | Independent review of the balanced checker and measurements |

## Verification scope

The new formal modules were compiled with **Coq 8.18.0 / OCaml 4.14.1** and
their selected assumption reports are closed. Recursive `coqchk` passed for:

- the generic `BalancedBisim` module and its dependencies;
- the concrete `MarkerInstances` module and its dependencies;
- `CantorCredit`.

The exact balanced source theorem was kernel-checked during compilation;
it was not included in the separate recursive generic audit.
No complete 237-source Rocq endpoint or full Lean endpoint was rebuilt here,
and the maintained Rocq 9.1.0 lane was not replayed.

The marker instances use a native arbitrary-tape model. Their compiled bridge

For another 215-state endpoint, M124/FM215 have the smallest new marker

# A balanced Rocq certificate checker for exact K215

This packet adds a **checked optimization of the existing source-correspondence
proof**. It does not change K215, its source program, the numerical calculus, or
the ZFC-refutation predicate. The inspected repository commit is
`53269bcab1efc0f82d3022645bd7cf0c22d84959`.

## New result

`Source215Balanced.p215_dagPerm_balanced` has compiled with Coq 8.18.0, with
closed assumptions:

```coq
forall R, rm_halts p215 ([], R) <-> rm_halts dagPerm ([], R).
```

The new checker uses a binary-indexed tree instead of `nth_error` over a list
of 2,240 certificate entries. The original plain checker's semantics and
soundness theorem are reused. `checkTree_flatten` proves exact equality with
the ordinary checker on the flattened tree, assuming its explicitly checked
size invariant. `tree215_exact` proves that flattening the constructed tree
returns the exact existing plain certificate; `tree215_valid` proves the size
invariant. The complete concrete forward check is evaluated and checked by
the kernel. Both programs are the unchanged repository definitions.

The new generic proof has **194 lines / 6,480 bytes**. The concrete exact-data
wrapper has 23 lines and the source theorem 21 lines. This is reusable proof
infrastructure; it is not advertised as a reduction of total proof-source
lines. Its purpose is to simplify the *checking workload* while preserving
the existing mathematical proof.

## Prior work retained rather than claimed again

The input packet `docs/incoming/ZFC215_Proof_Simplification_2026-10-21.zip`
already supplied compact positive-integer path codes, zero-offset ordinary
bisimulation, and a one-sided symmetry theorem. Another incoming packet
already supplied a complete ordinary Lean lane; a third normalized 2,240
checkpoints to 1,426. The present result adds the **Rocq balanced lookup** that
the first packet described as future work. It retains that packet's
`PathCodec.v`, `Cert215Compact.v`, and `BisimMirror.v` with attribution.

## Concrete reduction of lookup work

There are 2,239 decrement checkpoints, one halt checkpoint, and 4,479 queried
successors including the initial checkpoint. For these exact references:

| Representation | Traversal nodes visited |
|---|---:|
| List with `nth_error` | 5,018,706 |
| Balanced tree | 54,514 |

The ratio is **92.06**. This counts list/tree constructors visited in the
lookup component, not bit operations, program-path walks, segment simulation,
kernel work, or total runtime. The worst tree lookup visits 13 nodes, including
the leaf. `tree215_lookup_bound` proves that bound for **every** binary index,
including out-of-range ones. `lookup_metrics.py` reproduces the finite census;
the census is not an assumption of the correctness theorem.

For a balanced N-entry certificate with O(N) lookups, tree traversal has
O(N log N) node visits versus O(N^2) worst-case visits for the list. Here cuts
and indices are binary `N`, avoiding a hidden unary conversion at each lookup.
Charging linear cost for comparisons/subtractions on O(log N)-bit integers
gives O(N log^2 N) indexing bit operations. These bounds concern the indexing
component; program decoding and register-segment checking remain unchanged.

## Measured local comparison

On the shared execution environment, one matched run gave:

| Check | Plain list | Balanced tree |
|---|---:|---:|
| Coq `Time vm_compute` transaction | 16.008 s | 11.314 s |
| Complete source-module `coqc` process | 33.103 s | 24.772 s |

These illustrative observations correspond to 29.3% and 25.2% lower wall
time, respectively. They are **single observations in a shared environment**,
not stable benchmark claims. The balanced tree also takes 13.159 s to compile
its construction/exactness module. Therefore the data do not establish an
end-to-end first-build speedup, nor a complete endpoint-build speedup. A
production generator can emit the balanced tree directly while retaining the
exactness check as an independent audit target; that proposal is not measured
here.

## Verification scope

All dependencies used for this experiment were compiled from source during
this task; unchanged objects were reused only within this task while iterating
on the new module. Every selected new proof has a successful `coqc` kernel
check and a closed assumption report. The generic `BalancedBisim` module and
its dependency closure also passed recursive `coqchk`. The separately checked
recursive target does **not** include the large concrete source certificate.

The exact current `Prog215.v`, `DagPerm.v`, and original `Cert215Offsets.v`
were compared byte for byte with the corresponding incoming inputs; all three
match. The current bindings are recorded in `evidence/current_repo_binding.json`.
The source theorem itself needs no trust in the certificate generator: any
tree passing the verified checker proves the stated equivalence.

This packet does **not** replay all 237 Rocq sources, the complete binary/ZFC
endpoint, or the pinned Rocq 9.1 toolchain. The reported external theorem is
not an encoded proof in PA or ZFC's own proof syntax. The full endpoint's
mathematical composition remains available from the repository; production
adoption requires rebuilding the affected endpoint clients.

## Reproduce and integrate

With Coq 8.18.0 on PATH, from this directory:

```sh
python3 reproduce.py --output /path/to/empty/build
python3 lookup_metrics.py
```

Add `--benchmark` to compile the incoming plain-list baseline, or
`--check-generic` for the recursive generic audit. Proof compilers run serially
under the same lock. No Mathlib, network, binary proof cache, or complete ProveIt
checkout is required. The original Rocq 9.1 dependency source is retained; the
driver's 9.1 branch is an integration convenience and was not run here.

For integration, put the new modules in the desired K215 namespace, keep the
public name `p215_dagPerm`, replace its proof with the body of
`p215_dagPerm_balanced`, update the maintained generator, and rebuild
`Correct215` and `CorrectDense215` with assumption reports. Reuse the input
compact certificate and symmetry modules rather than maintaining duplicate
copies. The table, source program, and endpoint statements remain identical.

## Attribution

The new balanced checker and experiment are this packet's contribution.
The source semantics, original checker, K215 construction, numerical calculus,
set-theoretic calibration, compact path codec, ordinary source proof, and
symmetry theorem remain contributions of their respective authors. Existing
headers and the incoming packet's notices and license boundaries are retained
in `licenses/`. New material may be incorporated under ProveIt's terms.

# A checked finite certificate for the two-marker family

This directory replaces separate handwritten proofs for M124 and FM215 by
one generic, verified finite-table certificate. It also supplies M125, the
provider-125 instance already described as an option in the earlier M124
note. **Every table here has 215 working states. No 214-state result is claimed.**

## Checked results

`MarkerFold.v` (322 lines) proves `checked_fold`: when the finite Boolean
certificate is true, the two exact tables have equivalent halting behavior
from state 0, for every integer head position and every complete Boolean tape.
It also proves `timed_simulation`: each old n-step execution has a matching
new m-step execution with n <= m <= 3n, the same whole tape and head, and
the prescribed control identification.

`MarkerInstances.v` (35 lines, generated tables excluded) instantiates the
theorem for M124, FM215, and M125, and gives an explicit proposition-transport
corollary for M125. All three modules compiled under Coq 8.18.0 / OCaml 4.14.1.
Six printed theorem assumption reports are closed under the global context;
recursive `coqchk -silent MarkerInstances` also passed. The receipts and raw
logs are under `verification-final/`. There are no admitted or custom axioms.

The checker verifies all finite rows, equal table lengths, the two incoming
marker conditions, ordinary-row agreement under the state map, the local
three-step shapes, and halt stability. Its correctness theorem also covers
indices outside the finite row range. The construction needs no start-tape
or register invariant: both marker roles are noninitial, and every incoming
old transition writes the required predecessor marker.

## Exact concrete rule

The generic parameters for all three examples are

    a=124, b=127, halt=254, u=62, v=14, w=138, provider0=8.

Only `provider1` varies: 59 for M124, 109 for FM215, 125 for M125. The old
zero branches go from roles 124 and 127 to 62 and 14. Their one branches
both go to 138. Incoming rows write predecessor bits 1 and 0 respectively.
The new table merges the roles at 124 and uses 127 as a selector. On zero
it reads the predecessor and returns through an existing provider, preserving
all tape cells. The roles therefore take one or three new steps per old step.

M125 has the following four replacements relative to K215:

    110 0 0 R 124
    124 0 0 L 127
    127 0 0 R 8
    127 1 1 R 125

The file `M125.dense.tm` is the exact bijective relabeling to working labels
0 through 214 and halt 215. The mapping and both hashes are retained in
`M125.canonicalization.json`. This finite relabeling is audited in Python;
the compiled theorem uses the native table.

## Model and endpoint boundary

The native Coq tables have 303 list slots because some native labels are
sparse. Exactly 215 slots have two outgoing rows. `Halts` means reaching
the designated halt label 254 under a totalized step function that leaves
a configuration fixed on missing rows. The independently audited complete
working rows and transition closure exclude nonhalt holes from every run
starting at 0. Thus this predicate has the conventional TM meaning on these
literal tables. `put_standard` proves agreement with ordinary point updates;
sharing no-op writes avoids needing function extensionality.

These are compiled **table-to-table** theorems. A compiled bridge to the
repository's zipper/dense representation and composition with its complete
ZFC endpoint remain separate integration work. Ordinary composition with
the accepted exact K215 theorem is immediate after the representation
identification, and the elementary finite simulation is formalizable in
ZFC. The generic calibration corollary exposes the inherited calibration
as a theorem premise rather than pretending to prove it here.

## Reproduce

The finite exact-data and complete startup corroboration is:

    python3 verify.py --output /tmp/marker-finite.json

It checks all four literal tables against the generated Coq data, exact
state counts and target closure, the dense renaming, and every matching
boundary through the complete blank startup. For each variant, 95,714 old
steps correspond to 95,840 new steps, with 63 three-step blocks; the common
final configuration has control 84, head -8, and the same 95 one-cells.
This finite run is corroboration; the unbounded conclusion is the theorem.

To compile from fresh sources and run the recursive checker:

    python3 build.py --out /a/fresh/output/directory

The driver serializes compiler use. `generate_tables.py` checks exact literal
regeneration by default; its optional `--output` writes a new generated file.
Sources, tool identity, command status, logs, and object hashes are retained

# A concrete kernel proof of zero-credit enumeration

`CantorCredit.v` supplies a new standalone formalization of the ordinary
NIP-to-DROP injection already documented in ProveIt's ZC215 candidate. It
uses only the Coq/Rocq standard library. It is a contribution to proof
simplification, not a new 214-state construction or a complete ZC215
correctness endpoint.

## What is now proved

The actual pairing is `Cantor.to_nat (x,y)`, i.e.

    P(x,y) = ((x+y)(x+y+1))/2 + y.

The command fields are literal:

- `DROP`: `[0]`;
- `NIP`: `[1]`;
- `MP x`: `[2,x]`;
- `AX c x y`: `[c+3,y,x]`.

A word is explicitly nonempty. A terminal command is emitted with residual
zero; a nonterminal command with residual `1 + encode(tail)`. In particular,
`encode [DROP] = 0`. The executable decoder consumes at most `n+1`
recursive calls on input `n`, justified by the actual decreasing residual.
There are no hypotheses asserting unique parsing or monotonicity of an
unspecified codec: those properties are proved for these definitions.

The core closed theorems are:

- `encode_injective`: two command words with the same raw code are equal;
- `unique_raw_word`: every natural has exactly one nonempty command word;
- `encode_decode` and `decode_encode`: actual executable round trips;
- `concrete_tag_lowering`: changing a selected NIP to DROP strictly lowers
  the raw code, preserving the remaining commands and fields;
- `lower_injective`: this operation is injective on NIP occurrences, because
  replacing that same position back by NIP recovers its source;
- `exhaustive_schedule_zero_credit`: for every `n,j`, the prefix consisting
  of all candidates below `n` and the first `j` positions of candidate `n`
  has at least as many DROP as NIP occurrences;
- `exhaustive_credit_before_nip`: when position `j` of candidate `n` is NIP,
  the preceding prefix has strictly more DROP than NIP occurrences.

The predicates count occurrences, not distinct command values. Position and
word identity are retained. The last two theorems have no scheduler premises:
the schedule is constructed literally from the concrete decoder. The more
general intermediate `concrete_prefix_credit` theorem permits any finite
set of occurrences closed under complete earlier candidates.

The definition `schedule_cut n j` includes `j` positions of the current
candidate. If `j` exceeds its actual length, the extra positions have no
command and count neither way. A genuine syntactic execution prefix uses
`j <= word_length (decode n)`. This convention makes the final inequality
slightly stronger without changing its application.

## What remains before a ZC215 endpoint

This proof does not import or model the Turing transition table. To obtain
the machine endpoint one must separately establish:

1. the exact source implementation decodes these fields and continuations;
2. its actual candidate refill enumerates precisely 0,1,2,..., with no skipped
   return or wrong control target;
3. the command-level theorem-head invariant uses the proved prefix credit;
4. the source-to-binary positive simulation and complete startup frame;
5. the inherited numerical-calculus/ZFC consistency calibration.

The ordinary ZC215 packet already gives arguments and executable evidence
for those connections, but that is not a compiled endpoint supplied here.
A parser theorem alone does not validate a changed low-level return.

## Why this helps

The abstract prefix-credit file in `alternatives/gc-zc215/prefix_credit/`
leaves the key `lower_push`, `lower_earlier`, and `lower_injective` facts as
hypotheses. The present file proves them with the actual Cantor field
encoding, proves its exhaustive decoding, and constructs the concrete
prefix. Thus it supplies a small reusable semantic interface instead of
candidate-density estimates or finite reserve accounting. AX contributes
zero credit to this proof; no axiom-bundle stack length is assumed.

The primary K215 is still the least risky target for shortening the
already compiled complete proof: its initialized stack is zero, so its
existing safe-store invariant does not require this arbitrary-tail
argument at all. ZC215 is a useful independent semantic candidate, whereas
the M124/FM215 family is the simpler *relative* proof extension.

## Reproduce

From this directory:

    python3 build.py --out /a/fresh/output/directory

The driver serializes compiler access using `/tmp/proveit-proof-compiler.lock`,
compiles the exact source copy, runs recursive `coqchk`, and retains complete
logs and a source-hash receipt. The recorded toolchain is Coq 8.18.0 / OCaml
4.14.1. This is not advertised as a Rocq 9.1.0 replay. The standard-library
source imports contain no project-specific dependency or additional axiom.

The `verification-final/` logs are the final successful run; earlier local
compilation attempts are development history and need not be distributed.

`53269bcab1efc0f82d3022645bd7cf0c22d84959`. `CantorCredit.v` is an original

# Framed decoder blocks for exact K215

This component completes a local formal foundation of the incoming finite
decoder-product proposal. The data architecture is inherited; the generic Lean
proofs, executable checker and their concrete instantiation are supplied here.

## Statements

`FramedWindow.lean` defines finite known tape cells and an evaluator that rejects
before reading an unspecified cell. A proved refinement theorem lifts any
successful local execution to the complete integer-indexed tape. Its translated
form works at every head location. When the local block restores its cell list,
it restores the entire arbitrary tape, including the unspecified exterior.
The generic list semantics uses the first matching coordinate; duplicates do
not invalidate the theorem. Concrete windows have distinct consecutive cells.

`DecoderCertificate.lean` defines positive-duration blocks and a separate finite
structural checker for source nodes and decoder roles. A `Chain` relation carries
the exact window premise at every location. `chain_sound` concatenates any finite
chain using the full machine's run-addition law.

`K215Decoder.lean` contains the exact native table, 202 source DAG nodes, 234 roles,
and 281 distinct blocks. The product has 371 internal and 97 primitive-entry edges.
The block widths one, two and three have counts 252, 25 and 4; the maximum duration
is seven steps. All local windows include the currently scanned cell. The source
expands to the pinned 4,751 primitive occurrences.

The concrete `certificate_checked` combines all block checks with finite
structural checks. `restores_arbitrary_tape` and `certifies_block_chains` instantiate
the generic semantic results. Explicit malformed examples are rejected.

All three modules compiled afresh under Lean 4.32.0, commit
`8c9756b28d64dab099da31a4c09229a9e6a2ef35`, in 41.646 summed compiler seconds.
The literal block-acceptance theorem has no axioms. Semantic theorems use only
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. There is no `sorryAx` or
`native_decide`; the generator is not a logical premise.

The independent audit imports no generator. It binds all 430 native actions,
all source nodes and roles, and expansion to all 4,751 sites. It replays every
block, checks role reachability, and rejects malformed block/structural controls.
It also demonstrates intentional scope boundaries: structural validity alone
does not check positive duration or primitive argument semantics.

The expansion binding is currently ordinary Python evidence, not an in-kernel
identity with upstream `KSource215`. Theorems for source paths producing `Chain`
window witnesses, primitive semantics, register boxes, pointer returns and full
site coverage remain to be attached. This component does **not** replace
`KSites215`, prove the complete source runtime, or rebuild the ZFC endpoint.

# K215: the normalized source certificate now checked in Rocq

This package ports the 1,426-entry source certificate from the incoming Lean
normalization proposal to Rocq/Coq. It combines that certificate with the exact
K215 source definitions and the proved path codec and mirror helpers from the
incoming compact-source proposal. The new contribution is the **compiled Rocq
checker and its concrete all-register source theorem**, with a tested facade
that preserves the existing public source interface.

The exact incoming archives and hashes are recorded in `PROVENANCE.json`.
The normalized certificate, the idea of quotienting trailing zeros, the compact
path codec, and the plain mirror helper are prior work, not newly claimed here.

## Checked mathematical statement

`NormalizedSource215.p215_dagPerm_normalized` states:

```coq
forall R, rm_halts Prog215.p215 ([],R) <-> rm_halts DagPerm.dagPerm ([],R).
```

Both program definitions are byte-for-byte copies of the current repository at
`53269bcab1efc0f82d3022645bd7cf0c22d84959`. The statement is for every
natural-valued register file. It has no consistency premise. Its dependency
report and the generic checker report are closed under the global context.

This is the precise **source-correspondence layer** of the established K215
machine proof. The binary machine, boot frame, tape interpreter, numerical
calculus, and ZFC refutation predicate are unchanged. The complete 237-module
machine-to-ZFC endpoint is not rebuilt by this package.

## Actual verification result

The fresh twelve-module build completed successfully in 80.632 seconds of summed
compiler wall time, with a peak of 824,648 KiB (805.32 MiB). The separate recursive
`coqchk` of `NormalizedSource215` also completed successfully, in 521.235 seconds;
its exit code is zero. The primary driver therefore completed in 601.867 seconds
of summed proof-process wall time. The source module itself took 13.718 seconds,
including a forward VM reduction reporting 6.874 seconds.

The public facade and typed client compiled in a further 2.608 and 1.870 seconds,
respectively; both dependency reports are closed. A supplementary recursive check
of the generic checker also passed (44.191 seconds). The independent binding audit
passed for every serialized entry. There was no interrupted final recursive check.
These timings were not benchmarked against an old source proof.

`verification/compilation-summary.json` separates the twelve source compilations,
two interface compilations, and recursive checker results. The full raw receipts
and logs are retained. No complete machine-to-ZFC endpoint replay is claimed.

## What is smaller

| Representation | Entries | Uncompressed source bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production Rocq offset certificate | 2,240 | 1,499,170 |
| Incoming compact ordinary certificate plus path codec | 2,240 | 173,003 |
| This normalized ordinary certificate plus the same codec | 1,426 | 109,958 |

The reduction is 814 entries (36.3393%). The normalized certificate by itself
has 108,633 bytes; the retained codec has 1,325 bytes. The new generic checker
has 193 lines and 8,315 bytes; the concrete source theorem has 21 lines and
757 bytes. `metrics.json` gives the exact measurements and their scope. Source
byte counts do not measure proof-object size or checking speed. We did not run
a controlled timing comparison with either baseline.

The source proof requires one finite checker evaluation. It uses ordinary
register equality and no signed-offset layer. The converse follows from the
generic `ncheck_mirror` theorem. The shared JSON has one halt checkpoint and
1,425 decrement checkpoints, giving 2,851 branch obligations including the
initial branch.

## Why normalization is sound

For finite bit lists define `ipeq P Q` to mean that every bit agrees when the
lists are extended by false bits forever. The existing `RMEquiv.hn_ipeq` theorem
transfers a halting run of exactly N steps between equivalent pointers. Its
proof uses the interpreter's full consumed leaf path, including the zero bits
read beyond a shorter stored pointer.

The new Boolean `ibeq` checks this equivalence. `ibeq_ok` proves its soundness.
The normalized branch checker executes the original `seg` function on both
programs, checks equality of the register increment counts, and compares each
resulting pointer with its certificate representative using `ibeq`.

At each branch the inherited `seg_hn` and `seg_run` lemmas produce the actual
source and target segment endpoints. `hn_ipeq` transfers the source endpoint
to its stored representative. The corresponding target halting run transfers
back from its stored representative. The induction decreases at the next
register test, which consumes a genuine source step; zero-length segments do
not compromise this descent. The two possible test outcomes then use the
certificate's successor rows. Mirroring swaps the two pointers and the two
segment checks, so a second checker evaluation is unnecessary.

**The normalization caveat:** only trailing false bits in the mathematical
instruction-pointer representation are identified. The proof does not delete
an arbitrary suffix, operate break/continue on a shortened consumed path, or
remove physical cells from the binary Turing machine's tape frame. Those
would require separate theorems. All path arithmetic still uses the consumed
leaf path returned by the unchanged interpreter.

# Coordinated marker sharing toward 214 states

This supplement records a new bounded synthesis family and its negative result.
**It contains no accepted 214-state ZFC machine.** The eighteen input machines are
215-state reference machines, not new discoveries in this supplement. The
synthetic positive control is only an 11-to-10-state local gadget.

## Construction being tested

Suppose `(p,q)` and `(u,v)` are disjoint pairs of old controls. In each pair one
read branch is shared, and a bit next to the head distinguishes the two old
origins on the other branch. The two pairs use the same marker side. Merge
`q` into `p` and `v` into `u`, and add one fresh selector `H`.

At the changed branch of `p`, write tag 0 (or 1), move to the adjacent marker,
and enter `H`. At the changed branch of `u`, write the opposite tag, move to
that marker, and enter `H`. The selector preserves the marker and returns to
the tagged cell, entering provider `f0` or `f1` according to the marker. The
existing provider paths must restore the original tape effect and meet a
positive old execution with the mapped control and exactly the same head and
whole tape.

This reduces the count by one if it succeeds: `215 - 2 + 1 = 214`.

The temporary tag is the distinction from the earlier double-marker search.
Both source pairs may have their conflict on read 0, or both on read 1; the old
scanned bit need not itself identify the pair. Moreover, the C++ search runs
all four new rows together and allows provider paths to revisit the retained
merged controls and selector. The earlier strict-provider filter excluded
those revisits. The construction still has a restricted shape: it does not
synthesize arbitrary 214-state transition tables.

## Correctness obligation for a successful construction

Let `pi` identify the two deleted labels with their retained labels and fix all
other controls, including halt. The old machine has a finite-window invariant
`I` containing the blank initial configuration and closed under every old step
and both possible entering exterior bits. For each invariant window at an
affected old branch, require a positive old path and a positive new path that
end with control related by `pi`, identical head position, and identical tape.
No path may inspect a cell outside the window. The unchanged branches simulate
in one step. These obligations suffice for blank-start halting equivalence:
iterate the positive joined blocks along the deterministic old run. A finite
old halting run reaches halt after finitely many blocks because each consumes
at least one old step. An infinite old run gives arbitrarily long new prefixes
because each new block is also positive; no block can pass through halt. The
same synchronized blocks therefore exclude a finite new halt in the divergent
old case. Finite-window equality extends to the whole tape since the exterior
is untouched.

The invariant is sound by induction on the number of old steps. Its checker
verifies the initial all-zero window and each abstract successor. Entering bits
are universally quantified by the two checked alternatives. Abstract windows
need not be concretely reachable. Consequently, rejection at one such window,
a window escape, or a 64-step limit is only a failed certificate search; none
is by itself a concrete counterexample or a lower bound.

steps. Provider targets range over the 213 retained old working controls;
halt and the new helper are excluded as direct provider targets. Old and new
paths can nevertheless reach halt or revisit the helper through the trial's
rows. Both tag orientations are tested. The two originals in a pair have a
literally equal unmodified branch. Start is excluded from the four folded
origins. Each `families` count multiplied by `213^2` gives the assignment count.
A trial is rejected as soon as a context fails; every reported trial is still
a complete pair of provider assignments, not a count of individual row tests.
These are specifications, not a claim of pairwise distinct transition graphs.
The `first` log field counts trials passing the first context only and has no
correctness significance.

The eighteen input domains have **no absent state/read-symbol row**, even when
seeded with the actual blank window. The independent checker validates all
eighteen domains with a list-of-cells successor calculation, separately from the
inherited bit-mask worklist generator.

## Positive and negative controls

`positive-control.txt` describes a synthetic eleven-control table with two
pairs that both differ on read zero. The temporary tag enables one shared
selector to reduce its local gadget to ten controls. The C++ search finds the
intended row assignment. A separately implemented dictionary-tape simulator
checks every one of 32 local contexts: each old one-step effect agrees with the
new three-step effect. The gadget reads only offsets -1 and 0, so the untouched
exterior is arbitrary. Replacing one selector target causes 16 failures;
erasing the temporary tag causes 16 failures. These controls exercise both
origin selection and restoration of the overwritten scanned cell. They do not
establish anything about ZFC or about a complete blank-start synthetic program.

## Reproduction

Python 3 and a C++17 compiler are sufficient; no network, numerical solver,
Lean, or Rocq installation is required for this bounded search.

```
python3 verify.py --work /tmp/coordinated-marker-audit
python3 verify.py --work /tmp/coordinated-marker-replay --search
```

The default command decompresses the hash-bound invariants, independently
checks their closure, checks the source-table bindings and count arithmetic,
and runs the independent positive/mutation controls. `--search` additionally
compiles the delivered C++ source, reruns the synthetic discovery control and
all eighteen exact finite searches, and compares counts/hits with the saved logs.
The output directory must be fresh. Saved raw timings are incidental.
`code/local_invariants.py` is the inherited generator; an optional
`--regenerate` invocation recomputes its fixed points and requires byte identity
with each saved decompressed certificate.

## What this changes about the research direction

The searched family is more coordinated than one-state deletion or one-row
helper reuse: two pair identifications, a fresh selector, and both writes of a
temporary tape tag are active together. Its failure narrows that specific
family, while leaving source redesign, a different register/tape invariant,
changes to existing provider rows, nonlocal joins, and three-or-more-pair
sharing open. The search supplies no finite or universal lower bound on the
number of states needed for the consistency equivalence.
